question: Can recorded hearing impairment, major-noise interruptions, or wind differences explain the rainfall-associated expansion of the active frog community?
sample: same complete 10-stop matched wetter-drier route x RunNumber pairs as the metacommunity synthesis, restricted only by prespecified detection-covariate availability

stop_hearing_impairment.definition: If Massachusetts MassNoiseIndex is present, impaired=1 for index >=2 and 0 for index 0-1; otherwise use the regional Noise yes/no field when valid (1=yes, 0=no).
stop_hearing_impairment.protocol_basis: NAAMP regional programs could record ambient noise as yes/no or with the Massachusetts noise index; index >=2 corresponds to moderately or more strongly affecting sampling.

stop_timeout.definition: TimeOut==1 if a major noise disturbance caused the observer to break the 5-minute listening period; otherwise 0.

run_wind.definition: mean of numeric StartWind and EndWind Beaufort codes when both are available and within 0-5

run_level_derivation.hearing_impairment_fraction: mean standardized impairment indicator across the 10 sampled stops; require >=8 valid stops
run_level_derivation.timeout_fraction: mean TimeOut across 10 sampled stops; require >=8 valid stops
run_level_derivation.pair_covariates: wet minus dry for each run-level quantity

primary_models.formula: response ~ rain_contrast + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + hearing_impairment_difference + timeout_difference + wind_difference + C(State) + C(RunNumber)

car_count_2006plus.run_metric: mean numeric CarCount across sampled stops; require >=8 valid stops
car_count_2006plus.model: add wet-minus-dry mean car count to all three primary formulas

mass_noise_index.run_metric: mean MassNoiseIndex among valid 0-4 values; require >=8 valid stops
mass_noise_index.model: replace standardized hearing-impairment fraction with wet-minus-dry mean MassNoiseIndex while retaining timeout and wind

interpretation.if_supported: The rainfall-associated spatial, local-alpha and route-gamma signals are not explained by recorded survey hearing impairment, noise interruptions or wind differences.
interpretation.boundary: This is a measured-detection-condition robustness test, not proof that all acoustic detectability differences are absent.

prohibited: no outcome-dependent choice among noise encodings
no changing MassNoiseIndex threshold after readback
no excluding noisy surveys based on observed effect direction
